questions.q: You are about to tow a friend's car on a rope 9 metres long. What should you do?
options: You can drive: a long rope is safer than a short one
Shorten the rope so that there is 4-6 m between the vehicles
Shorten the rope to 2 m so that the vehicle does not swerve
You can drive if you switch on the hazard warning lights
questions.explain: When towing on a tow rope, the distance between the towing and towed vehicles must be within 4-6 m. On a rigid tow bar, it must be no more than 4 m.

questions.q: May you tow a passenger car on a tow rope if there is no one at its wheel?
options: Yes, if you drive at a speed of no more than 50 km/h
Yes, if the distance between the vehicles is no more than 4 metres
No, there must be a driver at the wheel of the towed vehicle
questions.explain: Towing on a tow rope or a rigid tow bar is allowed only when there is a driver at the wheel of the towed vehicle. Without a driver, it is allowed only on a special rigid tow bar that keeps the vehicle on the towing vehicle's path.

questions.q: You are towing a truck on a rigid tow bar. Which statement is correct?
options: Passengers are not allowed in the load body of the towed truck
Passengers may ride in the load body if the sides are closed
A driver is never needed in the towed truck on a rigid tow bar
Passengers may ride in the load body if the speed is no more than 50 km/h
questions.explain: When towing on a tow rope or a rigid tow bar, passengers are not allowed in a towed bus (trolleybus) or in the load body of a towed truck. A driver is needed at the wheel of the towed vehicle, except when the design of the rigid tow bar keeps the vehicle exactly on the towing vehicle's path ⟦47⟧.

questions.q: There is black ice outside. You only have a tow rope. May you use it to tow a broken-down car?
options: Yes, if you drive no faster than 30 km/h
Yes, if the rope is no longer than 4 metres
Yes, if both vehicles have their hazard warning lights switched on
No: towing on a rope is prohibited in black ice conditions
questions.explain: Towing on a tow rope is prohibited in black ice conditions. In such conditions, you may use a rigid tow bar or partial lifting.

questions.q: The steering of a car has failed. How may it be towed?
options: On a tow rope with a driver at the wheel
On a rigid tow bar no more than 4 m long
Only by raising the front or by partial lifting
By any method, if the speed does not exceed 50 km/h
questions.explain: It is prohibited to tow a vehicle with non-functioning steering. Only towing by raising the front or by partial lifting is allowed.

questions.q: The brakes are not working on a passenger car with an actual mass of 1500 kg. It is to be towed by another passenger car with an actual mass of 1800 kg. How can this be done?
options: On a tow rope
It cannot be done; such towing is prohibited
On a rigid tow bar
On any coupling, if you drive no faster than 50 km/h
questions.explain: Half of 1800 kg is 900 kg, and the towed vehicle weighs 1500 kg. Towing a vehicle with a non-functioning braking system is prohibited if its actual mass is more than half the actual mass of the towing vehicle. If the mass is less, only a rigid tow bar or partial lifting is allowed.

questions.q: You are about to tow a friend's broken-down car on a rope. An acquaintance of yours who has no driving licence wants to sit at its wheel. May you drive like this?
options: Yes: the engine of the towed car is not running
No: the towed vehicle needs a licensed driver
Yes, if the speed does not exceed 50 km/h
Yes, if he only steers and brakes
questions.explain: When towing on a rope, there must be a driver at the wheel of the towed vehicle ⟦48⟧, that is, a person who is driving it ⟦49⟧. You may not drive a vehicle without a driving licence ⟦50⟧, and handing over control to such a person is also prohibited ⟦51⟧.

questions.q: Your car is being towed on a rope. Its hazard warning lights are not working. What should be done?
options: Nothing: hazard warning lights are needed only on the towing vehicle
Switch on the main-beam headlights
Switch on the rear fog lamp
Fix a warning triangle to the rear
questions.explain: The towed motor vehicle has its hazard warning lights switched on ⟦52⟧. If it has none, or they are faulty, a warning triangle is fixed to the rear of the towed vehicle.

questions.q: Your friend, an experienced driver with a category B licence, offers to teach you to drive using his car on city streets. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, if your friend has more than 3 years of driving experience and there are no passengers in the car
Yes, if you put the “Learner vehicle” sign on the car
No: only a driving instructor may teach on the road
Yes, if you only drive on streets with light traffic
questions.explain: The instructor must have a qualification certificate and a licence of the required category ⟦53⟧. Training on public roads takes place only along routes agreed with the authorised body, and in the presence of a driving instructor ⟦54⟧.

questions.q: Learner driving is taking place in the city, with a driving instructor next to you. An acquaintance asks for a lift on your way. May you take him in the car?
options: No, learner driving allows no passengers
Yes, if he sits in the back seat of the car
Yes, if he already has a driving licence
questions.explain: Learner driving on the roads is allowed only with an instructor present, once the learner has basic skills, and with no passengers in the vehicle.

questions.q: What methods of towing motor vehicles do the Rules provide for?
options: Only on a rope or a rigid bar, with a driver
On a coupling, by raising the front, or by partial lifting
Only on a rigid tow bar and on a recovery truck's platform
By any method the towed vehicle can withstand
questions.explain: Towing is carried out using a coupling (flexible or rigid), or by raising the front part of the vehicle on a special support device of the towing vehicle, or by partial lifting onto its platform ⟦55⟧.

questions.q: What does towing by the method of partial lifting mean?
options: The towed vehicle is partly loaded onto the towing vehicle's platform
The towed vehicle is fully loaded into the load body of a truck
The towed vehicle is partly unloaded to make it lighter
Towing two vehicles at once on one coupling
questions.explain: With partial lifting, the towed vehicle is partly loaded onto the platform of the towing vehicle. A similar method is raising the front part on a special support device of the towing vehicle ⟦56⟧.

questions.q: In which case may a car be towed on a rigid tow bar without a driver at the wheel?
options: If the towing speed is no more than 20 km/h
If the towed car is lighter than the towing car
In no case: a driver is always needed
If the tow bar keeps it on the towing vehicle's path
questions.explain: Towing on a rigid tow bar or a tow rope is done only with a driver at the wheel of the towed vehicle. There is one exception: the design of the rigid tow bar ensures that the towed vehicle follows the towing vehicle's path when driving in a straight line ⟦57⟧.

questions.q: Your car is being towed on a rigid tow bar, and the distance between the vehicles is 5 m. Is this allowed?
options: Yes: on a rigid tow bar, 4 to 6 m is allowed
Yes, if the speed is no more than 50 km/h
No: on a rigid tow bar the distance must be no more than 4 m
No: on a rigid tow bar the distance must be at least 6 m
questions.explain: Here there are 5 m between the vehicles. On a rigid tow bar, the distance between the towing and towed vehicles must be no more than 4 m, while 4-6 m is the norm for a tow rope ⟦58⟧.

questions.q: Your car is being towed on a rope, and the distance between the vehicles is about 3 m. Is this allowed?
options: Yes: the shorter the rope, the safer the towing
Yes, if the rope is marked with flags or panels
Yes, if the towing speed is no more than 30 km/h
No: on a tow rope you need 4 to 6 m
questions.explain: On a rope at 3 m, the driver of the towed vehicle will not have time to react if the towing vehicle brakes sharply. On a tow rope, the distance between the vehicles must be within 4-6 m ⟦59⟧.

questions.q: According to the Basic Provisions, how is the flexible connecting link (rope) marked when towing?
options: With at least two red-and-white flags or panels
With one red flag fixed in the middle of the rope
With yellow reflective tape along the whole length of the rope
Not at all: the hazard warning lights on the vehicle are enough
questions.explain: Warning devices for flexible connecting links are flags or panels measuring 200 × 200 mm, with alternating red and white diagonal stripes 50 mm wide and a retroreflective surface. At least two such devices are fitted to the flexible link (Basic Provisions, para. 12).

questions.q: A broken-down bus is being towed on a rigid tow bar. May passengers stay inside it?
options: Yes, if the towing speed is no more than 50 km/h
No: passengers are not allowed in a towed bus
Yes, if there are no more than eight of them
Yes, if there is a driver at the wheel of the bus
questions.explain: When towing on a tow rope or a rigid tow bar, passengers are not allowed in a towed bus (trolleybus) or in the load body of a towed truck ⟦60⟧. A driver is still needed at the wheel of the bus ⟦61⟧.

questions.q: A broken-down truck is being towed by the method of partial lifting. May a passenger ride in the cab of this truck?
options: Yes, if he is wearing a seat belt
Yes, if the towing speed is no more than 30 km/h
No: riding in the cab of a towed vehicle is prohibited
Yes, but only during daylight hours
questions.explain: The towed truck stands at an angle on the platform, and it is dangerous to be in the cab. When towing by raising the front or by partial lifting, passengers are not allowed in the cab or load body of the towed vehicle, or in the load body of the towing vehicle ⟦62⟧.

questions.q: Where are passengers not allowed to be when towing by raising the front or by partial lifting?
options: Only inside or in the cab of the towing vehicle
In the towed vehicle and the towing vehicle's load body
Only in the load body of the towed truck
Nowhere, if the towing speed is no more than 50 km/h
questions.explain: When raising the front or using partial lifting, passengers are not allowed in the cab or load body of the towed vehicle, or in the load body of the towing vehicle ⟦63⟧. Riding in the cab of the towing vehicle is allowed.

questions.q: A truck is towing two cars at once on ropes, as shown in the diagram. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, if each rope is 4-6 m long
Yes, if the speed is no more than 30 km/h
Yes, if there is a driver at the wheel of each car
No: towing two or more vehicles at once is prohibited
questions.explain: In the diagram, the truck is pulling a blue car, and that car is pulling yours. Towing two or more vehicles is prohibited ⟦64⟧: such a “train” is hard to steer and brake.

questions.q: The brakes are not working on your car, which has an actual mass of 1200 kg. You will be towed by a truck with an actual mass of 4000 kg. How can this be done?
options: Only on a rigid tow bar or by the method of partial lifting
By any method, including on a rope
It cannot be done: towing with faulty brakes is not allowed
Only on a rope 4-6 m long
questions.explain: Half the mass of the truck is 2000 kg, and your car weighs 1200 kg, that is, less. In that case, towing a vehicle with a non-functioning braking system is allowed, but only on a rigid tow bar or by the method of partial lifting ⟦65⟧.

questions.q: You are riding a motorcycle without a sidecar, and another motorcycle like it is about to tow you on a rope. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, if the rope is 4 to 6 m long
Yes, if you use a rigid tow bar
No: such towing is prohibited
Yes, if both riders are wearing helmets
questions.explain: A two-wheeled motorcycle easily loses balance when a rope jerks it. That is why towing by a motorcycle without a sidecar, and towing of such a motorcycle, is prohibited ⟦66⟧.
